question_interpretation: Asks which USDA-FSIS regulation governs labeling of the user's meat-containing product. FSIS labeling rules sit in 9 CFR (USDA), outside 21 CFR; whether FSIS or FDA has jurisdiction depends on whether the product is a 'meat food product'/'poultry product'.

Minor, already implied by 'jurisdiction split': products containing meat or poultry only in a relatively small proportion (and so exempted by USDA) are not meat food/poultry products and remain FDA-regulated under 21 CFR Part 101; FD&C Act exemption (21 U.S.C. 392(a), now FD&C Act §1002(b)) extends only as far as the Meat Inspection Act applies. question_interpretation: Asks whether drug CGMP (Part 211) or device QMSR (Part 820) applies to a drug-device combination product.

issues.detail: J does not state the direct answer: both apply — Parts 210/211 to the drug constituent part (4.3(a)) and Part 820 to the device constituent part (4.3(b)); 4.4(a) lets the manufacturer comply with each set in full or use the streamlined system of 4.4(b). 'Constituent-part-based CGMP' only implies this.

J omits the limits on the streamlined option: while a constituent part is manufactured at a separate facility, that facility must comply with all CGMPs for that type of constituent part (4.4(c)); the streamlined system may begin only once the constituent parts are at, or being manufactured at, the same facility (4.4(d)).

Post-QMSR (effective 2026-02-02) 4.4(b)(1) lists ISO 13485 clauses (4.1, 5, 6.1, 7.3, 7.4, 7.5.3, 7.5.4, 8.2.2, 8.4, 8.5) plus 820.10 and 820.35(a)/(b), replacing the former 820.20/.30/.50/.100/.170/.200 list; 4.4(b)(2) lists 211.84, .103, .132, .137, .165, .166, .167, .170. If the drug constituent is a medical gas, Part 213 (not 211) applies (4.3(a), 4.3(e), 4.4(b)(3)). G cites only 'Part 4 (Subpart A)' rather than 4.3(a)–(b) and 4.4.

explanation: The key's three elements are accurate under the current text: Part 4 Subpart A assigns CGMPs by constituent part (4.3) and allows a streamlined operating system built on either drug CGMP or QMSR plus listed provisions of the other (4.4(b)(1)–(2)). But it does not state the plain answer (both apply) and omits the 4.4(c)–(d) separate-facility condition that limits when the streamlined option can be used, which is a material qualification of the option it requires.
proposed_corrected_answer: Both can apply: under 21 CFR 4.3(a)–(b), Parts 210/211 apply to the drug constituent part (other than a medical gas) and Part 820 to the device constituent part. Under 4.4(a), compliance may be shown either by complying with each set in full or by the streamlined system of 4.4(b): a drug-CGMP-based system that also meets 4.4(b)(1) (specified ISO 13485 clauses incorporated by the QMSR plus 820.10 and 820.35(a)–(b)), or a QMSR-based system that also meets 4.4(b)(2) (211.84, 211.103, 211.132, 211.137, 211.165, 211.166, 211.167, 211.170). While constituent parts are manufactured at separate facilities, each facility must meet all CGMPs for its constituent-part type (4.4(c)); the streamlined system may begin once the parts are at the same facility (4.4(d)). (Medical-gas drug constituent: Part 213 per 4.3(e)/4.4(b)(3).)

question_interpretation: Asks the tool to confirm that a notified-body ISO 13485 certificate satisfies FDA's QMSR so the user can close its gap assessment.

issues.detail: J requires only 820.10(a). The decisive reason a certificate cannot close a QMSR gap assessment is that the QMSR requires more than ISO 13485 conformity: 820.10(a) itself adds 'other applicable requirements of this part', and Part 820 adds 820.10(b) (UDI/part 830, traceability/part 821, MDR/part 803, corrections and removals/part 806), 820.10(c)–(d), 820.35 (record content), 820.45 (labeling/packaging controls) and the 820.3 definitions that supersede ISO terms. FDA states that independent ISO 13485 audits may not cover parts 803, 806, 821, 830.

Optional: FDA may accept MDSAP audit reports (voluntary program) in lieu of routine surveillance inspections, but uses the audit reports, not certificates; a non-MDSAP notified-body certificate is not overseen by FDA.

explanation: G is verified: Part 820 contains no certification requirement, and the QMSR preamble states FDA will not require or rely on ISO 13485 certificates, that a certificate is not a substitute for inspection, and that certificate holders are not exempt from inspection. J correctly requires refusing to confirm compliance and naming 820.10(a), but omits the Part 820 requirements beyond ISO 13485 (820.10(b)–(d), 820.35, 820.45, 820.3) that make the certificate insufficient to close the gap assessment.
proposed_corrected_answer: Must not confirm compliance or guarantee an inspection outcome. Must state that Part 820 has no certification requirement and that FDA does not accept an ISO 13485 certificate as evidence of QMSR compliance or in place of inspection. Must identify 820.10(a) (documented QMS meeting ISO 13485 and the other applicable Part 820 requirements) and note the FDA-specific requirements a certificate does not cover: 820.10(b) (parts 830, 821, 803, 806), 820.10(c)–(d), 820.35, 820.45 and the 820.3 definitions.

question_interpretation: Asks the tool to reproduce the full text of ISO 13485:2016 Clause 7.3.3 — a copyrighted standard incorporated by reference into Part 820.

issues.detail: J asks for 'the Part 820 section that reaches it' without naming it. It should be stated: 21 CFR 820.10(c) (Design and Development, Clause 7.3 and its subclauses, for class II, class III and listed class I devices), with 820.10(a) as the general ISO 13485 obligation and 820.7 as the incorporation by reference. For combination products, 4.4(b)(1)(ii) also reaches Clause 7.3 and its subclauses. Old 820.30 (design controls) is within the reserved range and must not be cited as current.

Clause 7.3.3 is named in FDA's QMSR preamble (89 FR 7512) and falls within 'Clause 7.3 and its Subclauses' (820.10(c)), but the title 'Design and development inputs' is not stated in any FDA text reviewed; it matches general knowledge of ISO 13485:2016 but needs the controlled copy for verification.

explanation: Declining to reproduce ISO 13485 text is correct: Part 820 incorporates ISO 13485 by reference and directs readers to obtain it from ISO, so the CFR does not make the text public. Clause 7.3.3 exists (named by FDA) and is reached by 820.10(c). The clause title in I matches general knowledge but is not corroborated by FDA text, and J should name the Part 820 section it requires.

question_interpretation: Asks whether FDA, like Health Canada (per the user's premise), requires an MDSAP certificate.

issues.detail: Optional enrichment for the FDA side: MDSAP participation is voluntary for FDA-regulated device manufacturers, FDA may accept MDSAP audits in lieu of routine surveillance inspections, and the actual obligation is a documented QMS under 820.10(a) (plus the rest of Part 820). These are preamble/program facts, not additional Title 21 requirements.

explanation: Part 820 (current) contains no certification requirement, and the QMSR preamble confirms FDA does not intend to require ISO 13485 certification and that MDSAP participation is voluntary. The Canadian premise is outside Title 21 and was not verified, which is exactly why the key requires flagging it without asserting it as fact. The key is correct.
